full_judgment:
On an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the petitioner the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18-2-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 affirming those dated 16-3- 1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, incharge, Singair, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 should not be set-aside. 

 2. The facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that opposite party No. 1 as petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 against the petitioner and others for setting aside the auction sale arising out of Execution Case No.4 of 1975 in pursuance the exparte judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No.4 of 1974. The further case is that he was a Government servant and was posted at Barisal. While he was serving at Barisal without his knowledge and without serving any notice upon him, an ex parte judgment was passed against him on 19-3-1974 and thus Execution case No.4 of 1975 was filed and the present petitioner auction purchased the valuable property of him. The said auction was confirmed on 25-11-1975. The said auction was not in proper, illegal and malafide and the value of the auction money was not proper. The opposite party No.1 came to know the same on 11-078-1976. Hence the case. 

 3. The case was contested by the present petitioner and the predecessor of the opposite party Nos. 4-13 by filing joint written objection stating interalia that the case of the present opposite party No.1 is false, malafide and barred by limitation. The present opposite party had knowledge about the money suit and decree execution case and auction matter. The auction was never secret and it was sold by open tender. The present opposite party No.1 would not conduct the said Miscellaneous Case and the uncle of the present opposite party No. 1 namely Safiuddin conducted the Miscellaneous Case. The auction purchaser (present petitioner) got the delivery of possession through Court and since then the auction purchaser has been possessing the suit property. The case of the present opposite party No.1 is false and liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record allowed the said miscellaneous case and setting aside the order of auction dated 25-11-1975 in Money Execution Case No.4 of 1975 by his judgment and order dated 16-3-1994. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court, the present petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 before the District Judge, Manikganj. The said appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Manikganj who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record dismissed the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment of the trial Court by his judgment and order dated 18-2-1999. 

 7. Mr M Asif Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that both the Courts committed error of law resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the summons was duly served upon the opposite party in Money Execution Case No.4 of 1975 .The learned Advocate further submitted that both Courts below did not consider that the miscellaneous case filed. by the opposite party was barred by limitation since Exhibit-"Kha" proves that the opposite party No. 1 had knowledge about the auction since 2-4-1974 thus they committed error of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the Courts erroneously found that there was a irregularity in the auction sale but did not consider that the petitioner got possession over the suit land immediately after the auction sale but the opposite party did not take any initiative at the earliest stage but long after ten years he filed this suit which is absolutely barred by limitation thus both the Courts committed error of law resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice. Thus, he prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 8. On the contrary Mr Md lalaluddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 (a)-l(c) submitted that both the Courts concurrently found that the auction which was held by violating the provision of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the Courts concurrently found that the notice which was published in a local newspaper but such type of paper has no existence even the present petitioner did not submit the original newspaper thus both the Court concurrently opined that the auction was held by committing fraud upon the Court and since both the Courts found fraud in the auction deed in such a case the limitation is immaterial. The learned Advocate further submitted that concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional .Jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his argument he relying the decisions of the case reported in 32 DLR 168 and 43 DLR (AD) 82. Thus, he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the Courts below, papers and documents as available in the records. In the instant case it appears that the Money Suit No. 4 of 1974 was decreed ex parte which was filed for realization of Taka 1,200 thereafter, the petitioner filed Money Execution Case No. 4 of 1975 and accordingly the auction was held and auction was confirmed on 25-11-1975. The opposite party No.1, the petitioner of the Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 claimed that without any summons and following procedure of law the said auction was held. It appears that the trial Court after discussion of the evidence on record and the procedure of proclamation and the auction of the property found that the same was conducted without following the procedure of law even the ex parte decree which was passed without summons of the petitioner of the Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984. The appellate Court concurred the said finding of facts and both the Courts found that by which substantial injury resulting from the irregularity is proved thus, the Courts below setting aside the auction procedure. It also appears that the trial Court found that the publication of the proclamation in the local Newspaper (Exhibit-"Ka") has no existence in the locality and there is no declaration number, the publisher, the auditor etc and thus clearly opined that which is a fabricated documents. Since both the Courts found that the auction was held by practicing fraud upon the Court so the said concurrent finding of facts cannot be interfered with in revisional application. 

 10. It is well settle principle that the limitation is immaterial when any order obtained by practicing fraud upon Court. This proposition supported by the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman reported in 50 DLR(AD) 205 where in their lordships held. 

 11. It is settled principle that concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional application when there is no misreading or misappropriation of facts. This proposition supported by the decision of the case of Shambhu Nath Poddar vs Bangladesh Railway reported in 43 DLR (AD) 82 wherein their lordships held - 

 12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and discussions above I find no merit in the Rule. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, without any order as to cost. The impugned Judgment and order dated 18-2-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 affirming those dated 16-3-1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, in-charge, Singair, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 are hereby upheld.
